Shadow of the Tomb Raider is a visually stunning main campaign experience - Despite having some bugs and glitches as you begin your new adventure, Eidos Montréal does the near-impossible feat of concluding the Survivor Trilogy with an impressive game that prioritises classic puzzle-solving over action-heavy set-pieces that were highlights of the previous two games.

The best art style and art direction I've ever seen in a game. The combat is so satisfying that even if you rage quit, you'll probably come back to it because no other game compares. And somehow there isn't a single bad voice performance across all 29 characters.

My only complaint is that you really start to notice how poorly balanced the game is after a few successful escapes--and when you have to start cranking up heat levels in order to go for 100%, your average player will have to rely pretty hard on RNG in order to get any viable run.

Could’ve been an awesome game.
The new mechanics with the arrow + jump + falcon take some time to get used to, but they’re nice.

The game itself is pretty easy. You can’t really die in boss fights; you just get thrown out of the arena.

What really bothers me when playing is the CONSTANT FPS drops. I mean every 3-5 seconds. It averages 30 FPS the whole game and gets close to 15 FPS when hunting bosses (you have to chase them across the map, which I guess loads a lot of chunks and makes the game unplayable).
I have never seen such ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ performance in a game.
The publisher and developer don’t really look like they want to fix this, which is a shame, because the game’s kinda fun.

Definitely not worth the full price. I paid R$20 (roughly $4), which is more than I would ever pay for a game like this.

The bonus weapons in the DLCs were pretty nice, using a Gravity gun is always fun. Plasma rifle rules, grenades are also handy. Rockets vs. rockets. Includes obligatory train rides. I am coming back to this game after 4-5 years and (DESPITE IT'S ANNOYING WAY OF HANDLING DIFFICULTY), it has some of the smoothest platforming I have ever played. The visuals are absolutely phenomenal, and the soundtrack is practically transcendent. Although its runtime is incredibly short, it is worth each and every second of your time. The abilities feel smooth and responsive, each one goes together near perfectly, and even when you only have a third of them, you still feel like you're one with the character once you get the hang of the movement.

TL:DR: Phenomenal game all around, but do be aware that the later areas end up feeling more tedious and annoying than actually difficult (I'm looking at you, Sorrow Pass).

I’ve been trying to get the Platinum for a while now, and I’m running into the same problem both here on Steam and on Epic. You complete the achievements (whether they’re collection-based, challenges, or even the ones you’re supposed to get automatically as you progress through the story) and yet the game still won’t award them to you, no matter how many times you try again or reinstall the game.

Amazing.
A very successful sequel. Anyone who loved the first game will also love Part II. In fact, it took me twice as long to finish Part II as it did to finish Part I. The setting: wonderful. The music: wonderful. The story: take a guess.

A few puzzles are actually very easy. Others, on the other hand, require a bit of out-of-the-box thinking. There are some new creatures, some great new ideas, and a story that gets a bit darker and dives deeper than in Part I.

I can sincerely recommend this game to anyone who likes puzzle-platformers (that aren’t extremely difficult), loved Planet of Lana, and doesn’t mind eagerly waiting for Part III after finishing the game.
